whyItMatters: MD5 is broken for security purposes: collisions are practical, so it cannot protect passwords, signatures, or untrusted-data integrity.
actions: Decide the purpose: security use (passwords, signatures) or plain checksum (deduplication, etags).
For security uses, switch to SHA-256 or better; for passwords use bcrypt, scrypt, or argon2.
Leave a comment where MD5 remains for non-security checksums so future scans stay quiet.
verification: No MD5 call remains on a security path; remaining uses are commented checksums.

example.caveat: Password hashing needs a slow KDF (bcrypt/scrypt/argon2), never a fast hash — including SHA-256.
